title: ABPM Clinical Informatics Board Prep
subtitle: Everything you need to pass the boards, taught the way you'd actually want to learn it
summary: A complete board-prep course for the American Board of Preventive Medicine subspecialty exam in Clinical Informatics. Eight modules cover the four ABPM domains: fundamentals, clinical decision making and care process improvement, health information systems, and leadership/change management. The point is not to memorize trivia. The point is to build a working mental model strong enough that the exam questions feel obvious.
learningOutcomes: Define clinical informatics and locate it precisely against bioinformatics, public health informatics, and consumer health informatics.
Read an HL7 v2 message and a FHIR resource and explain what each is doing and why one replaced the other.
Map a real EHR workflow and identify where the sociotechnical system is brittle.
Design a clinical decision support intervention that satisfies the CDS Five Rights without creating alert fatigue.
Critique a quality dashboard for both statistical validity and frontline usability.
Explain HIPAA, HITECH, and the 21st Century Cures information-blocking rule in terms a clinician will actually act on.
Lead an EHR change effort using a named change-management framework and defend the choice.
Pass the ABPM Clinical Informatics board exam.
prerequisites: Clinical training (MD, DO, or equivalent) or substantial clinical exposure.
Comfort with basic statistics (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values).
